currentContext.business: Indian Oil Corporation Limited refines crude oil, transports it and its products through an extensive liquid pipeline network, and markets petroleum products across India through a nationwide retail and bulk distribution network. Alongside the core refining-pipelines-marketing chain, the Company operates verticals in Petrochemicals, Natural Gas, City Gas Distribution, Alternative Energy, Exploration & Production, Explosives and Cryogenics, supported by a growing international footprint. It serves domestic retail motorists and highway users, industrial and bulk customers, fertiliser units, aviation customers, City Gas Distribution networks and the Armed Forces.

currentContext.expansion: IndianOil is running an infrastructure expansion programme anchored on three strategic pillars - Strengthening Core Businesses, Accelerating Green & Clean Energy, and Embracing Future-Ready Diversification. Capital expenditure of Rs 32,405 Crore (including equity investments of Rs 663 Crore) was incurred during 2025-26, a figure the Company says has grown nearly 2.2 times over the past decade. Over 170 projects, each with capex exceeding Rs 5 Crore, are in various stages of execution with a cumulative capex of over Rs 2.5 Lakh Crore, undertaken on a standalone basis as well as through joint ventures and subsidiaries, to be financed through a prudent mix of internal accruals and borrowings. In REFINING, multiple brownfield expansion and integration projects are under implementation with the objective of raising commissioned group refining capacity from 80.75 MMTPA currently to around 98 MMTPA by 2027-28; the major expansion projects at Panipat, Gujarat and Barauni refineries, plus the PX-PTA complex at Paradip, are described as progressing well. In PETROCHEMICALS, the Rs 5,894 Crore Acrylics/Oxo-Alcohol Complex at Gujarat Refinery, a 153 KTPA Butyl Acrylates complex and a 260 KTPA Group-III base oil project at Haldia Refinery are intended to build presence in specialty chemicals, premium lubricant base stocks and high-value downstream products. In PIPELINES, key projects under implementation include the 2,730 km Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG Pipeline through a joint venture (among the world's longest LPG pipeline systems), conversion of the Mundra-Panipat Pipeline linked to refinery expansion, and the Kochi-Kanyakumari-Thoothukudi natural gas pipeline for southern India; the network is being augmented with over 1,600 km of new capacity, alongside storage infrastructure, automation and preparation for the Government's CBG blending programme. In MARKETING, the retail network of over 42,800 outlets is being expanded and repositioned into an integrated multi-energy mobility ecosystem through Transformative Retail Outlets, CPCL's 'Sooper' branded outlets, 'Apna Ghar' facilities (378) and Wayside Amenities (87), EV charging, CBG dispensing and non-fuel retail. In LPG, infrastructure expansion includes the Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG Pipeline, new bottling plants and supply infrastructure in remote and underserved regions. In GAS, the Company is expanding LNG sourcing/trading, regasification, CGD, Auto LNG and industrial gas. In UPSTREAM, it is expanding domestic and overseas exploration blocks. In GREEN & CLEAN ENERGY, construction has commenced on India's first large-scale 10 KTPA Green Hydrogen Plant at Panipat Refinery; a 100 KTPA HEFA-based SAF plant at Paradip Refinery is planned through a proposed joint venture structure; JV IndianOil NTPC Green Energy Pvt. Ltd. is on course to commission 50 MW of RE capacity this year against a planned 650 MW round-the-clock renewable power requirement for refinery expansion projects; 467 retail outlets were solarised during the year taking the total to 36,341 outlets and ~180 MW of installed solar at retail; and under SATAT the Company held 559 active CBG Letters of Intent with 49 plants established including 5 commissioned during the year. Terra Clean Ltd (TeCL) has land aggregation under progress in Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh and achieved an 'AA' credit rating from CARE. Water infrastructure is being extended - treated wastewater already supplied to Mathura Refinery from an 8 MLD STP and Gujarat Refinery from a 20 MLD STP, with plans to extend a similar arrangement to Haldia Refinery through a 3 MLD STP by 2027-28.
currentContext.mdna: India is expected to remain the largest contributor to incremental global oil demand over the next decade, with demand projected to increase from about 5.5 mb/d to nearly 8 mb/d by 2035, and India's overall energy requirement expected to more than double by 2050 - supporting long-term opportunities across refining, marketing, pipelines, petrochemicals, natural gas, aviation fuels and downstream infrastructure.|In India, petroleum product demand has grown at a CAGR of 5.6% over the last five years; domestic petroleum product consumption rose 1.7% to 243.2 MMT in 2025-26, with Motor Spirit up 6.5% to 42.6 MMT and High-Speed Diesel up 3.6% to 94.7 MMT.|Transport and aviation fuel growth: rising vehicle ownership, road infrastructure, freight movement; ATF consumption reached a record 9.16 MMT, up 2.0% and over 8% above pre-pandemic levels; India is among the world's fastest-growing aviation markets.|Petrochemical import-substitution headroom: India depends on imports for nearly 45% of its petrochemical requirements and per capita consumption at around 15 kg is roughly one-third of the global average; domestic capacity is projected to reach about 55 million tonnes by 2035 and the market to expand to USD 375 billion by 2027 and nearly USD 1.25 trillion by 2040.|Gas-based economy expansion: gas demand projected to approach 135 bcm by 2035, supporting investment across LNG sourcing, regasification, pipelines, CGD and downstream infrastructure; CGD remains a key growth segment supported by network expansion and rising CNG adoption. FY26 saw a temporary correction - consumption fell an estimated 3.9% to around 68.5 bcm on elevated H1 spot LNG prices - but the medium-term outlook remains constructive as prices ease and new LNG supply comes online.|Electrification: global electricity demand projected to increase by over 40% by 2035; India added a record 51 GW of renewable capacity and 3.7 GW of large hydro in FY 2025-26 to reach 274.7 GW total, against a target of over 600 GW by 2032; renewable generation up 22% to 310 TWh, share of generation up from 13.9% to 16.8%.|EV adoption as both an opportunity and a demand headwind: EV registrations exceeded 2.5 million units in FY 2025-26 with penetration rising to 8.5% from 7.7%; electric two-wheelers were nearly 58% of EV sales and electric passenger vehicles grew approximately 86%; public charging infrastructure expanded to more than 27,000 stations, supporting multi-energy retail formats.|Digitalisation, AI and data-centre-led energy demand creating incremental opportunities across power supply, cooling fuels, lubricants, gas-based backup systems and renewable integration.|Shipping and marine fuels: India's growing trade volumes, expanding port infrastructure and strategic location support marine fuels, LNG bunkering and lubricants; lower-emission shipping fuel adoption supports LNG, biofuels and green methanol demand.|Policy tailwinds: National Green Hydrogen Mission with an outlay of Rs 19,744 Crore (green ammonia auctions, refinery hydrogen projects, incentives for 3,000 MW p.a. of electrolyser manufacturing, hydrogen hubs) and the National Critical Minerals Mission (Rs 7,280 Crore rare-earth magnet programme and a Rs 1,500 Crore recycling scheme). Ethanol blending in petrol achieved the 20% national target by March 2026.|Structural India context: fossil fuels account for nearly 93% of total primary energy supply; India is the world's third-largest energy consumer; installed refining capacity of 258.1 MMTPA makes it the second-largest refining hub in Asia and fourth globally, with refinery throughput up 1.3% to 272.1 MMT.|THREAT - rising geopolitical risk and supply disruption: West Asia developments and the Strait of Hormuz, through which nearly 20% of global oil and LNG trade flows, drove volatility across crude, gas, freight and insurance markets; product imports fell 7.9% to 46.8 MMT and exports fell 5.6% to 61.4 MMT on cargo rerouting and logistical constraints.|THREAT - high import dependence: India's crude oil import dependence has increased to around 88% (crude imports up 0.9% to 245.4 MMT while domestic crude production fell to 28 MMT from 28.7 MMT), and growing gas demand is expected to raise LNG import requirements, exposing the sector to supply concentration risk, currency fluctuation and external disruption.|IHB Ltd. risks.risk: Rising geopolitical risk and disruption of critical energy corridors
risks.note: Geopolitical tensions, trade fragmentation, sanctions and disruptions across critical energy corridors influence global energy markets. Developments in West Asia and around the Strait of Hormuz - through which nearly 20% of global oil and LNG trade flows - drove volatility across crude oil, natural gas, freight and insurance markets. The Directors' Report states directly that despite excellent FY26 performance, 'escalation of geopolitical disruptions may have an adverse impact on profitability of 2026-27', and that the fag end of 2025-26 saw prolonged disruptions to the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz and significant dislocations in global supply chains for petroleum products and LPG.

risks.risk: High import dependence and supply-security concentration
risks.note: India's crude oil import dependence has increased to around 88%, and growing gas demand is expected to raise LNG import requirements over the medium term. Dependence on imported crude oil, LNG, petrochemical feedstocks and critical minerals exposes the business to supply concentration risk, currency fluctuation and external market disruption - raising the importance of diversified sourcing, resilient logistics and long-term supply arrangements. Crude sourcing, supply-chain continuity and foreign exchange exposure are named as key risks the Company actively managed during the year.

risks.risk: Energy price volatility and margin uncertainty
risks.note: Global energy markets are increasingly characterised by short-term price volatility rather than stable pricing cycles. The correction in India's gas consumption during H1 2025-26, driven by elevated LNG spot prices, demonstrated how sensitive demand is to commodity prices. Such volatility influences procurement strategies, inventory management, project economics and capital-allocation decisions - directly relevant for a company whose refining margins are also listed among the key risks managed during the year.

risks.risk: Petrochemical margin pressure from global oversupply
risks.note: Large-scale petrochemical capacity additions in China and the Middle East continue to pressure global utilisation rates and margins. Naphtha-based producers - which is IndianOil's position - remain exposed to feedstock cost volatility and to competition from gas-based producers benefiting from lower-cost ethane and LPG feedstocks. Prolonged oversupply may continue to affect profitability across commodity petrochemical value chains, a structural headwind against the Company's petrochemical expansion strategy.

The energy transition brings stricter environmental regulations, carbon-related trade measures, fuel-quality requirements and disclosure obligations. Emerging frameworks on emissions, carbon intensity, sustainable fuels, shipping and industrial decarbonisation may increase compliance requirements, affect competitiveness and require additional investment in cleaner technologies and operating systems.

Increasing frequency and intensity of heatwaves, floods and other climate events present operational and infrastructure risks across the energy value chain. Rising cooling-driven electricity demand, pressure on power systems and weather-related disruptions increase the need for resilient infrastructure, storage and operational flexibility; rapid renewable expansion also requires continued investment in transmission, balancing mechanisms and grid stability.

risks.risk: Changing global trade flows, emerging energy blocs and critical-mineral / technology supply-chain dependence
risks.note: Regional supply alliances, export controls, sanctions and strategic competition across energy technologies may alter trade flows, investment patterns and technology access. Separately, the shift toward batteries, renewables, electrolysers, semiconductors and digital infrastructure increases dependence on critical minerals whose global supply chains (lithium, cobalt, nickel, rare earths, batteries, clean-energy equipment) remain highly concentrated geographically - a new form of strategic vulnerability, trade risk and price uncertainty for IndianOil's transition investments.

risks.risk: GOVERNANCE / OVERSIGHT GAP - board risk committees discontinued for want of Independent Directors
risks.note: This is a company-specific structural risk disclosed in the Directors' Report itself. The Company has an ERM framework and constituted a Risk Management Committee (RMC) of the Board, but 'due to non-availability of any Independent Director on the Board, the RMC has been discontinued w.e.f. March 28, 2026', as was the Audit Committee. Board-level risk oversight now rests on the management-level Risk Management Compliance Board (senior management personnel headed by the Chief Risk Officer), because changes to the Risk Register require RMC approval and periodic updates go to the Audit Committee and Board. Appointment of directors vests with the Government of India through MoP&NG, so remediation is outside the Company's control.

risks.risk: Fraud and internal-control incidents at operating locations
risks.note: 7 instances of suspected fraud by employees were reported during the year. Three were below Rs 1 Crore (POL pilferage through tank trucks of Rs 19.04 Lakh at Panipat Marketing Complex; Rs 39.17 Lakh of vendor-bill splitting to bypass approvals at North Guwahati Bottling Plant; Rs 39.60 Lakh of fraudulent vendor/contractor payments at Chittoor Terminal). Four exceeded Rs 1 Crore and were reported by the Statutory Auditors to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (POL pilferage of Rs 1.37 Crore at Kandla FST; Rs 1.41 Crore via manipulation of dip measurements at Pathankot AFS; Rs 1.53 Crore of fraudulent vendor payment at Gujarat Refinery; Rs 6.00 Crore of fraudulent payment to engineering contractors under Karnataka State Office). Investigations and disciplinary action are ongoing in some cases. The recurring pattern - product pilferage and circumvention of procurement/payment procedures across dispersed terminals, bottling plants and refineries - is a structural control risk for an asset- and location-dispersed distribution business.

As on March 31, 2026 there were twenty-two pending C&AG audit paras from performance, compliance, thematic and proprietary audits, on subjects including short realisation from disposal of land, an abandoned E&P project, grade-wise costing of petrochemicals, extra cost from delay in tender finalisation, PMUY benefits to unentitled persons, avoidable entry tax, updation of daily price change at retail outlets, recovery of turnover tax, expenditure turning infructuous from non-adherence to pollution clearance requirements, spectrum utilisation, MSME procurement, infructuous expenditure on a low-hydrocarbon and risky E&P block, supply logistics of petroleum products, idle investment in plant, infructuous expenditure on financing an inoperative pipeline, and various employee-benefit matters. Offsetting this, the C&AG issued NIL comment on the FY26 supplementary audit - the 20th consecutive year - and the Auditors' Report contains no qualification or adverse remark.

risks.risk: Operational safety, cybersecurity and regulatory compliance
risks.note: Explicitly named by the Board among the key risks proactively managed during the year, alongside crude sourcing, supply-chain continuity, forex exposure and refining margins. The Company cites cyber threats as a feature of its operating environment and manages these through its diversified sourcing strategy, infrastructure network and continuous monitoring mechanisms, supported by an internally developed ERM portal for enterprise-wide risk tracking.

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.
